title: Error Investigator: payload-first playback pane for debugging failed requests
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: design a compact, payload-first 'playback pane' that surfaces failed requests, retry behavior, and a taxonomy-driven error explorer so engineers can triage production failures from the Console without leaving the UI. Problem: current Console error views scatter logs, network details, and payloads across pages; engineers often need to jump to raw logs or GitHub to reproduce issues. This pane should prioritize the request payload and model response, allow deterministic replay of the request (with redacted secrets), show retry chain and fallbacks, and link to rollout/route policies and metrics. Deliverables: Figma prototype of the pane and interactions, high-fidelity microcopy for error taxonomy and copy for CTA buttons (Replay, Create Issue, Open in Playground), accessible states for empty / obfuscated payloads, and handoff notes for frontend and backend engineers about required APIs and sample payload shapes.
acceptance_criteria: Playback pane attaches to any failed request row in the Request List and opens as a right-side slide-over
Pane shows request metadata (timestamp, route, model, duration), request payload (structured viewer with syntax highlighting), and tokenized response preview
Playback supports a safe replay flow that redacts sensitive fields and warns users before execution
Retry chain visualization renders in a single line timeline with status badges (failed, retried, fallback) and links to logs
Error taxonomy selector filters related failures and surfaces common root causes and suggested remediation text
Visible links to rollout/A-B config and model variant used in that request
Design spec includes responsive behavior, keyboard accessibility, and ARIA roles for the pane and replay controls
decisions: Place the pane as a right-hand slide-over to avoid disrupting existing dashboards
Make payload the primary column with an expandable structured JSON viewer and a collapsed raw view
Introduce a one-click 'Safe Replay' that enforces redaction rules and requires confirmation
Use an error taxonomy dropdown (Network | Model | RateLimit | Validation | Internal) as the first-level filter
Show retry chain inline with micro-interactions to expand each attempt details
tradeoffs: Slide-over keeps context but reduces horizontal space for long payload fields vs. a dedicated full-screen page
Showing full unredacted payloads speeds triage but increases risk; we default to redacted with opt-in reveal
Embedding replay increases Console responsibility; we limit replay to sandboxed network calls and require audit logging
Adding an error taxonomy requires mapping telemetry to categories which will need R&D heuristics and may miss edge cases initially
reviewers_feedback: PM (Liam O'Connor): Likes payload-first approach; asks for an explicit link to rollout policies and impact estimation
Eng (Priya Kapoor): Requests API contract for 'replay sandbox' and a list of redaction rules; flags performance implications of rendering large payloads
SRE (Noah Park): Requires that any UI-initiated replay be rate-limited and logged to the audit pipeline
Design lead (Aisha Raman): Suggests stronger visual affordances for retry chain and clearer microcopy for the 'replay' confirmation dialog

notes_for_engineers: API expectations: /requests/:id returns metadata, structured payload, tokenization map, attempt list with timestamps and status
Redaction: use KMS-backed rules; strip PII and secrets before returning payload to the UI
Replay: POST /requests/:id/replay with sandbox flag; response should return simulated tokens and cost estimate; require feature flag gating
Telemetry: emit replay_initiated and replay_result events to the audit service with user id and request id
